chunks: And that which was narrated is: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abu al-Husayn al-Nakh'i from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"A cow suffices for five people at Mina if they are people of one dining table (i.e., a single household/group)."

key_terms.أَهْلَ خِوَانٍ وَاحِدٍ: People of one dining table (a single household or group sharing meals)
key_terms.بِمِنًى: At Mina (the location of Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: How many people can share one cow for sacrifice during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic consensus that a single cow suffices for five participants in the Hajj sacrifice, contingent upon their shared domestic unit (*ahl khawan wahid*). It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding communal obligations, distinguishing between individual and collective liability during the rituals at Mina.
